study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Chan et al., Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Social behavior in ASD males: The interplay between cognitive flexibility, working memory, and functional connectivity deviations

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction clearly states the goal to test whether between-network resting-state functional connectivity deviations from normative trajectories map onto social behavior in ASD males, and to examine whether executive function mediates those associations using ABIDE data. These statements directly articulate the study objectives and the intended application of normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “We posit that social behavioral problems observed in children with ASD are attributed to deviations in between-network rsFC from the established norm. To test this hypothesis, we used data from the ABIDE consortium… We first generated normative trajectories… We then aligned these normative charts to rsFC measures of 418 males with ASD… Next, we examined the associations between rsFC deviations and distinct domains of social behaviors… we also examined whether executive function mediated the association…”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort comprised non-ASD males aged 5.1–14 years from ABIDE I/II, with site-specific inclusion/exclusion criteria listed in Supplementary Table 1 and motion-based quality control (framewise displacement >0.9 mm or global BOLD changes >5 SD flagged as outliers). Final training/testing sample sizes for controls (321/77) are provided. However, reasons for exclusion at each site or after QC are not detailed, so eligibility and QC standards are partially but not fully documented.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Data for the current study were from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and ABIDE II… only males between ages 5.1 -14.0 years were included… The study dataset was then split into training and testing datasets. The training dataset was composed of 80 % of non-ASD males, while the testing dataset was composed of the remaining 20 % of non-ASD males and ASD males.” “Supplementary Table 1 summarizes the site-specific inclusion and exclusion criteria.” “Scan volumes with framewise displacement above 0.9 mm or global BOLD signal changes above 5 standard deviations were identified as potential outliers.”

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age was modeled with a smoothing function, mean relative motion was included as a covariate in the GAMs, and multi-site effects were addressed via ComBat harmonization (neuroCombat v1.0.13), satisfying consideration of demographic and site covariates.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: “Mean relative motion was included as a co-variate of no interest.” “To account for site effects, we employed the ComBat harmonization method… with the neuroCombat package v1.0.13.”

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort data source is explicitly identified as ABIDE I and II, a public dataset of ASD and control participants.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Data for the current study were from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and ABIDE II collections of the ABIDE initiative… a publicly available dataset…”

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Imaging data come entirely from existing ABIDE datasets (secondary use), and the item specifies NA for secondary data.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: “Data for the current study were from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and ABIDE II… a publicly available dataset…”

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They detail preprocessing using CONN Toolbox v20b with SPM12 realign/unwarp, slice-timing correction, motion/global signal outlier detection, normalization, segmentation, smoothing, nuisance regression, and band-pass filtering, indicating a specified pipeline and QC handling.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: “Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) data was processed… using the CONN Toolbox v20b… Scans underwent realignment with SPM12 realign & unwarp… Slice-timing correction… Scan volumes with framewise displacement above 0.9 mm or global BOLD signal changes above 5 standard deviations were identified as potential outliers… data were normalized… smoothed… nuisance variables… removed… band-pass filtered to… 0.008 and 0.09 Hz.”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The dataset was partitioned with 80% of non-ASD males for training and 20% for testing, and normative models trained on the training set were applied to the held-out testing set, fulfilling internal partitioning.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “The study dataset was then split into training and testing datasets. The training dataset was composed of 80 % of non-ASD males, while the testing dataset was composed of the remaining 20 % of non-ASD males and ASD males.” “Normative models were then applied to the testing dataset (n = 77 non-ASD males; n = 418 ASD males) to derive deviation scores (z).”

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: All modeling and application used ABIDE data only; no independent external healthy dataset beyond ABIDE was used for validation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “Data for the current study were from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and ABIDE II…” (only source described).

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify using generalized additive models (mgcv v1.8-42) with age smoothing and motion covariate, assessed via GAM.check, and applied to predict FC and compute z-scores, providing model type and key settings.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: “Normative trajectories were modeled with Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) for the training dataset using the mgcv package v1.8-42… a smoothing function was applied to age… Mean relative motion was included as a co-variate… The suitability of model parameters was assessed with the GAM.check function.”

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper describes fitting GAMs and applying them to derive deviation scores but does not report quantitative performance metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage) for the normative models on training or testing data.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Normative trajectories were derived for each between-network rsFC based on data from the training dataset… These models were then applied to the testing dataset… and the deviation between the predicted FC and actual FC in the testing dataset was calculated.”

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Table 1 reports sample sizes and demographics (age, IQ, SRS, BRIEF, motion) separately for the training controls (n=321) and testing controls (n=77), providing characteristics by partition.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: “Table 1 Phenotypic characteristics… Training N = 321… Testing (Control) N = 77…” with age, IQ, SRS, BRIEF, and motion values listed.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and library versions are provided (R 4.3.0, mgcv v1.8-42, PMA v1.2.1, mediation v4.5.0, CONN v20b, neuroCombat v1.0.13, SPM12), and data availability is stated. However, no code, trained model files, or access instructions beyond public data are provided.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: “All statistical analyses were conducted in R v4.3.0… mgcv package v1.8-42… PMA package v1.2.1… mediation package v4.5.0.” “Resting-state fMRI… processed… using the CONN Toolbox v20b… SPM12…” “To account for site effects, we employed the ComBat harmonization method… neuroCombat package v1.0.13.” “Data for the current study is publicly available.”

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical participants (ASD males) were drawn from ABIDE I/II with site-specific inclusion/exclusion criteria listed in Supplementary Table 1, and motion outlier handling described. Final ASD sample size (n=418) is given, but reasons for exclusion and QC attrition are not detailed.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “Data for the current study were from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and ABIDE II… only males between ages 5.1 -14.0 years were included… n = 816… testing dataset… ASD males [n = 418]. Supplementary Table 1 summarizes the site-specific inclusion and exclusion criteria.” “Scan volumes with framewise displacement above 0.9 mm or global BOLD signal changes above 5 standard deviations were identified as potential outliers.”

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses relating deviation scores to social behavior and mediation by executive function did not report adjusting for clinical covariates such as medication status, illness duration, or comorbidities; the methods only describe including SRS and BRIEF scores as outcomes/mediators without additional clinical covariates.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: “Sparse canonical correlation analysis… Only ASD patients were included in this analysis.” “We then examined if executive function significantly mediates the association between between-network deviation scores and social behavioral problems… focused on VANxDMN_z… BRIEF.”

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort is specified as ASD participants from the ABIDE I/II datasets, which are publicly available.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “Data for the current study were from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and ABIDE II collections… a publicly available dataset of participants diagnosed with ASD and age-matched non-ASD participants.”

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Table 1 provides sample size for ASD testing cohort (n=418) and reports age, IQ, SRS subscales, BRIEF scores, and motion, fulfilling demographic and clinical characteristics reporting.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: “Table 1… Testing (ASD) N = 418… Age at scan… Full IQ… Social Responsiveness Scale… BRIEF - Global Executive Composite… fMRI Mean Relative Motion (mm).”

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures are described, including the SRS (65-item parent-rated scale with five subscales and T-scores) and the BRIEF (86-item questionnaire with eight subscales and GEC T-scores), with scoring details.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: “The SRS… consists of 65 items… five subscales… Items are scored on a 4-point Likert scale… T-scores… used in our analyses.” “The BRIEF… 86-item questionnaire… eight clinical subscales… Higher scores indicate poorer executive function… Raw scores were linearly transformed to obtain T-scores, which were used in our analyses.”

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define deviation z-scores as reflecting individual atypicality from the normative mean and report that more positive deviations are associated with greater social behavioral problems. However, explicit thresholds or categorical definitions for atypicality are not provided.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: “Deviation scores (z)… reflect the individual degree of between-network FC atypicality from a typically developing population mean.” “Thus, a more positive deviation was associated with greater problems with social behavior.”
